history.predicted_effect: Validation R² about +0.001 to +0.002 over C187, with a slightly longer run.

history.hypothesis: Gated (tanh*sigmoid) dilated convolutions model multiplicative motif interactions. Summed skip connections from every layer give the readout features at all receptive-field sizes at once, from single motifs to whole-insert grammar. With C134's Student-t PC-target recipe this should approach the leader without per-output FiLM.
history.predicted_effect: Validation mean R2 around 0.829 (range 0.822-0.836). It should train stably, with a best epoch around 30-50 and SK-N-SH the weakest cell type as usual. Epoch time should be similar to or below C134.

history.hypothesis: Average pooling the deepest map at 30 positions dilutes the presence and strength of individual TF motif hits. Pooled taps from every stage let the head see single-motif evidence at full resolution beside the deep context features. Max pooling at the early stages records the strongest motif hit, and average pooling records motif counts.
history.predicted_effect: Validation R2 of about 0.831, roughly 1.5 floors below C134. Per-epoch time is about half of C134's, because there is no per-output dilated stack. If the taps help, the gain should show most in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, the cell-specific part, rather than in K562.

history.hypothesis: The dilated ResNet reaches about 60 bp per position but sees no global sequence context inside the trunk, and adding local depth did not help. A cheap squeeze-excitation gate, initialised to identity, lets each block reweight channels using the whole window (as LegNet does) without slowing early convergence.
history.predicted_effect: Epoch time rises under 10%, and the learning curve tracks C165 through epoch 50. The final score lands between 0.833 and 0.837, about C165 plus 0.3 floors, which is roughly 0.2 floors below C134.

history.hypothesis: The new part of this structure is the ref/alt pair-delta MSE, carried over from L40 at its default weight of 0.5 and never tuned on this trunk. Most single-base deltas are small, so in whitened PC space the term is probably small next to the var^0.25-scaled Student-t NLL plus 0.2*MSE. Doubling it to 1.0 should make the shared trunk resolve single-base effects more strongly, and that carries into absolute-activity predictions on unseen variant windows. This answers the fair-trial question of how much the delta term can add here.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R2 changes by about +0.0003 (roughly +0.1 noise floor). The effect is most visible in K562 and HepG2, where label noise is lower. There is real risk that the noisy deltas over-regularise.

history.hypothesis: The pooled FiLM embedding misses motif co-occurrence. C170's windowed bilinear pair features carry that, and they can lift the dilated FiLM leader if added through a zero-init path that does not slow early training.
history.predicted_effect: At epoch 50 it is within 0.3 points of R² of C188's curve, so it is not cut. Final score 0.835-0.838, most likely about +0.1 floor over C188. Any gain should be largest in K562 and HepG2. Epoch time rises by 10-20%.

history.hypothesis: The pair-delta term made the strongest gain on residual (non-LegNet) trunks (C188, +0.45). L43's plain ResNet is also residual, so supervising the ref/alt allele difference should sharpen single-base sensitivity there as well and give a small gain in the shared embedding.
history.predicted_effect: Score near 0.8355-0.836, within a floor of C170 (0.8354), with epoch time 1.3-1.8x C174's. SK-N-SH and HepG2 should move by no more than 0.002 R² in either direction.

history.hypothesis: Raising plateau_patience from 3 to 6 is the settings change with the most consistent record. It gained in five lineages: +0.49 (C131), +0.32 (C147), +0.31 (C152), +1.11 (C180) and +0.63 (C192). It lost slightly in two: -0.06 (C141) and -0.31 (C190). A 12-layer gated WaveNet with zero-init residuals starts as a near-shallow net and grows its depth gradually. Halving the LR after only 3 flat epochs probably cuts its high-LR phase short, so this trunk should benefit at least as much as the average lineage. This departs from the leader's settings, which keep patience 3. The leader's other difference, hnll_beta 0.25, was within noise when tested (C139, -0.18), so this edit tests the better-supported change instead.
history.predicted_effect: Training runs longer before the first LR halving. The best validation epoch comes later and mean R2 rises by about 0.001 to 0.002, to roughly 0.833 to 0.834.

history.hypothesis: Raising plateau_patience from 3 to 6 is the change that has gained most often across lineages: C131 +0.49, C147 +0.32, C152 +0.31, C180 +1.11 and C192 +0.63 floors. The SE gates start at identity and add input-dependent channel scaling, so they likely need more epochs at high LR before the first LR halving. A longer patience gives them that time. On the non-SE dilated trunk (C141) the same change was neutral (-0.06). The difference here is the extra gating, which may adapt more slowly than the trunk itself.
history.predicted_effect: Training runs longer at peak LR and the best epoch comes later. Mean R² rises by about 0.001 over C196, mostly in the cell-type contrast axes.

history.hypothesis: The allelic-delta term's contribution saturates with a few dozen pairs per batch. Most single-SNP deltas are near zero and dominated by measurement noise, so extra pairs add mostly noisy gradient and compute.
history.predicted_effect: Epoch time falls from about 92 s to about 75 s. The validation score lands within ±0.5 floor of C172 (0.8350), with the best epoch at a similar point.

history.hypothesis: Raising plateau_patience from 3 to 6 is the change with the widest support in this run: +0.49 (C131), +0.32 (C147), +0.31 (C152), +1.11 (C180), +0.63 (C192), against -0.31 (C190, L43) and -0.06 (C141). This lineage adds the ref/alt pair-delta term, which C172 showed is a slow-converging extra signal, and that should make longer high-LR phases more useful here than on C174. This edit is the trial's best shot at showing the structure at its best.
history.predicted_effect: Validation R² of about 0.833 to 0.834, a small gain over C199's 0.8325 from more epochs at each LR level before the first halving.

history.hypothesis: Untied depth does not help (S31), possibly because added parameters overfit the 40% subsample. One dilated bottleneck reused for 12 steps gives a large receptive field and deep iterative refinement with few trunk parameters (about 1.6M in all). The per-step BN and step embedding let each iteration specialise cheaply. That should match the untied dilated stack while regularising better.
history.predicted_effect: Lands below the leader at about 0.829 to 0.834; best guess 0.8325 (about -1.3 floors). Most of the loss should be in SK-N-SH and the contrast components, with the K562/HepG2 shared axis closer to the leader. Epoch time is similar to C188.

history.hypothesis: S14's ceiling near 0.834 for LegNet models comes from the LegNet trunk itself (depthwise EffBlocks with concatenated residuals), not from the readout or recipe. Putting that trunk under L46's dilated FiLM stack and recipe should therefore drop the score toward LegNet's level.
history.predicted_effect: Score about 0.8320 to 0.8345, roughly 1.5 floors below C195 (0.8355). The SK-N-SH R2 drop should be similar to the other cell types, since the trunk is shared. Epoch time should be similar or slightly lower.

history.hypothesis: Many single-base ref/alt deltas are smaller than their measurement noise. With equal weights, the delta term mostly fits noise. Inverse-variance weighting concentrates it on well-measured pairs, so it can sharpen allelic sensitivity without pulling toward noise.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R² within about ±0.003 of C188, most likely +0.0005. If there is a gain it is largest in K562/HepG2, where se is smaller relative to the deltas; SK-N-SH does not gain. Epoch time and convergence epoch stay unchanged.

history.hypothesis: The leader's per-output part reads only the final residual state of four dilated bottlenecks. Multiplicative tanh·sigmoid gating with a skip sum gives the readout direct access to every dilation scale, per output. This may lift the per-output specialisation that S52 calls the limit.
history.predicted_effect: Score within about one noise floor of C188: most likely 0.833-0.836, roughly 1.1-1.3x epoch time. SK-N-SH, the most cell-specific output, should gain or lose most.

history.hypothesis: L43's bilinear readout pools motif co-occurrence over the bottleneck. Adding L36's 60-bp plasmid flanks, with each outer flank blanked half the time in training, gives the readout insert-boundary context. The blanking keeps the model from leaning on the constant flank, and at eval it sees the full flank.
history.predicted_effect: Roughly neutral: about 0.834-0.836, a mean gain of -0.2 floors, with epochs about 1.3x slower. If it gains, the gain shows mostly in SK-N-SH.

history.hypothesis: LegNet's fourth max-pool leaves only 15 positions before the global average pool, which coarsens motif position and spacing information. The two trunks that pass 0.835 (C188, C170) keep 30 positions. Removing the last pool lets the final EffBlock stage and the mapper see twice the resolution.
history.predicted_effect: Validation R² about 0.8355, roughly +0.2 floors over C172, with the gain mostly in SK-N-SH and HepG2. Epoch time rises by about 15 to 25%. It should not be cut at epoch 50, because the parameter count is unchanged.

history.hypothesis: The leader may overfit sharp, non-smooth responses to small input changes, because many training sequences are near-duplicates (variant pairs and shifted windows). A VAT term penalises the change in prediction under the most sensitive L2 perturbation of the one-hot input (eps 2, about 0.13 rms per element). This should regularise the sequence-to-activity map toward smoother functions and help held-out chromosomes, most of all in the noisy SK-N-SH output.
history.predicted_effect: The run reaches about 0.834-0.837 (central estimate about 0.3 floors below C188). SK-N-SH R² should move most. Epochs should take about 1.6-1.9x as long, and the best epoch should come somewhat later.

history.hypothesis: Auxiliary linear readouts of the pooled features after stages 2 and 3 should do two things. First, they push intermediate layers to encode activity directly, which acts as a regulariser and a gradient shortcut on 107k-step training. Second, they speed early convergence of a fresh trunk, which S57 says decides survival. The readouts are discarded at prediction, so the model stays a single network.
history.predicted_effect: The run converges faster in the first 10 epochs than L46's first run. It finishes around 0.831 to 0.835 mean R2, about 1.5 floors below C188, with the per-cell pattern unchanged and SK-N-SH lowest. The auxiliary loss falls well below the label variance but stays above the main MSE.

history.hypothesis: The allelic-delta term is limited by heavy-tailed, noisy measured deltas, whose squared error dominates its gradient. A Huber error keeps the useful signal from the many small deltas while bounding the influence of noisy large ones.
history.predicted_effect: Same epoch time as C172. Score about 0.8352 (from +0.0 to +0.001), with most of any gain in SK-N-SH, the noisiest cell type. It is not cut early.

history.hypothesis: This answers S52. Doubling the shared trunk depth did nothing (C179), and readout additions hurt (C197). The remaining untested capacity is the per-output FiLM path, which runs once per cell type on 30 positions. Widening the dilated bottleneck mid width from ch//2 to ch and the mapper and head from 512 to 768 gives cell-specific features more room. SK-N-SH is the cell with the most specific signal, so it should gain most. Zero-init residual BN and zero-init FiLM keep the start identical to C188's dynamics.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R2 of about +0.0006 over C188, mostly from SK-N-SH. Epoch time rises about 15-25%. The best epoch stays in the 60-80 range.

history.hypothesis: S1 says LegNet stopped gaining once widened past about 3M parameters. If width saturation is general, widening this leader's shared conv stages by about 1.2x (the per-output dilated FiLM part left fixed) will not raise the score. If instead the shared motif features are the limit, the score will rise.
history.predicted_effect: Validation mean R2 within one noise floor of C202 (0.835-0.840), most likely about 0.837. Per-cell Pearson moves by under 0.003 and epoch time rises about 1.3x.

history.hypothesis: VAT (virtual adversarial training) on the one-hot input gave +0.55 floors on the dilated FiLM leader (C202, L46). On this LegNet trunk it should smooth the prediction surface near training sequences in the same way and cut overfitting on the 40% training set. This answers S62. The edit starts from C210 (Huber pair error, last max-pool kept), not from C208 as S62 suggests, because the edit start was drawn from candidates within a floor of the best.
history.predicted_effect: Validation R² rises about 0.0015 to 0.002 over C210, to about 0.8345. Epochs are about 35% slower, roughly 120 s each.

history.hypothesis: L45's shortfall comes from its shared-head readout rather than its DenseNet trunk. Under L46's dilated FiLM stack, VAT and pair-delta, the dense trunk's feature reuse should then match the plain residual stages.
history.predicted_effect: Slower early convergence and a final score of about 0.833-0.836. That is roughly 1 floor under C202, with the per-cell R² ordering kept (SK-N-SH lowest). Epoch time is similar or up to 1.2x.

history.hypothesis: L43's plateau near 0.835 is set by overfitting of the sharp bilinear readout to local input directions. VAT's local-smoothness penalty, which lifted C188 by 0.55 floors in C202, should regularise the pair-pool readout in the same way.
history.predicted_effect: Validation R2 of about 0.8360, roughly 0.2 floors above C170 (0.8354). The gain should be spread across the three cell types, with epochs about 1.3-1.5x slower. A score of 0.834 or lower would mean VAT does not transfer.

history.hypothesis: Fine-grained motif detail at full resolution, motif-pair spacing at middle resolutions and coarse grammar at 30 positions can all inform each other if every resolution stays alive and exchanges features repeatedly. Leader-style trunks discard fine resolution after max-pooling. Zero-init cross links let the net start as a plain ResNet chain, so it should converge at the usual pace.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R2 about 0.830 to 0.834, roughly 2.5 floors below C202. Epoch time about 1.0 to 1.3 times the leader's without VAT or pair-delta. If it gains, the gain should show most in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, the contrast-heavy cell types.

history.hypothesis: C182 widened the stem to 128 channels with kernel 15 and gained +0.42 floors on L36, a LegNet-branch, distributional-regression model with the same trunk, branches, mixup and HL auxiliary head. This lineage still uses the narrow 64-channel, kernel-11 stem. A wider and longer first layer should capture more motif and spacing detail before the first pooling, and that adds to the shared-axis signal that pair deltas also depend on. Nothing else changes, so the effect can be attributed to the stem.
history.predicted_effect: About +0.3 floors over C210, with slightly slower epochs (around 5 to 10%). The gain should be roughly uniform across the three cell types.

history.hypothesis: C216 uses the loss default hnll_beta 0.5, while the leader runs 0.25. The fair trial asks to try the leader's settings where a structure differs without a stated reason. A lower beta re-weights the Student-t NLL less toward high-variance rows. That should give more weight to the bulk of well-measured sequences, which dominate validation R².
history.predicted_effect: A small gain, about 0.3 noise floors, around 0.835.

history.hypothesis: plateau_patience 6 gained over its parent in 6 of 7 lineages (C152 +0.31, C180 +1.11, C192 +0.63, C198 +0.22, C200 +0.13, C203 +0.87; C190 -0.31). It holds the peak LR longer before halving it, which lets a new, larger trunk with EMA reach a better basin. The HRNet trunk is deeper, has many zero-init cross links and is newly initialised, so it is the kind of model that benefits from more time at full LR. The run still stops after 10 epochs without gain, so the cost is bounded.
history.predicted_effect: Validation R2 about 0.001 above C217's 0.8380, with the best epoch reached later.

history.hypothesis: L46's distinguishing part is per-output depth: a dilated bottleneck stack run once per output on shared weights, each layer followed by a per-output FiLM. Placed on HRNet-1D's coarsest stream, it lets each cell type refine long-range features before readout. The other streams stay shared, so the cell-type-specific part of the signal gains capacity without disturbing the shared multi-resolution features.
history.predicted_effect: Validation mean R2 within about half a floor of C217 (0.836-0.840), with a slight lean upward. Most of any gain should be in SK-N-SH and the contrast directions, while the shared-axis accuracy stays unchanged. Epoch time should rise by under 20%.

history.hypothesis: L40 is limited by overfitting to sequence-level idiosyncrasies, not by capacity. A VAT consistency term smooths the predictor in its most sensitive input direction, as it did on C202, and should lift validation R² on unseen chromosomes.
history.predicted_effect: Against C210 (0.8328), a gain of about +0.3 to +0.6 floors, landing near 0.8340 to 0.8345. That is slightly below C208's 0.8354. Epoch time should rise about 1.3x. The largest per-cell gain should be in SK-N-SH, if any.

history.hypothesis: plateau_patience 6 is the most replicated settings gain in this run: +0.31 (C152), +1.11 (C180), +0.63 (C192), +0.22 (C198), +0.13 (C200) and +0.87 on the same family (C203, L50). The one loss was -0.31 on L43's C190, which had no VAT. Here, VAT plus the Student-t heteroscedastic loss make validation improve more slowly and unevenly, so patience 3 likely halves the LR too early. Waiting longer at a higher LR should let the EMA weights settle at a better point.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R² up by about 0.001 (about 0.3 floors) to about 0.837, with a longer run before the first LR cut.

history.hypothesis: HRNet-1D's full-resolution stream gives it more input sensitivity than the pooled ResNets. VAT's smoothness penalty along the most sensitive input direction should regularise it as it did the dilated FiLM ResNet (C202). The gain should come mostly in late epochs, after the EMA has settled.
history.predicted_effect: Validation mean R² of 0.8395 to 0.8425, centred near 0.8407, about +0.1 floors over C221. Per-epoch time should rise by about 1.4 to 1.7x. Early epochs should be slightly behind C221 but within the epoch-50 cut.

history.hypothesis: A bidirectional LSTM over the 30 pooled conv positions models the order, orientation and spacing of motif combinations sequentially. This is a different inductive bias from dilated convolution or attention, and may capture motif grammar that the convolutional trunks miss, particularly the smaller cell-type-specific signal.
history.predicted_effect: It trains stably, because the recurrent path starts at zero, and finishes around 0.832-0.837, below the leader's 0.8404. I expect the gap to be smallest on the SK-N-SH and contrast components.

history.hypothesis: S1 says width is saturated on this trunk. The final shared stage width (320) is untested, and it sets the residual width of the per-output dilated FiLM stack, where cell-type specialisation happens. If that stage is the bottleneck, widening it to 448 should help. If S1 holds, the change should be flat.
history.predicted_effect: Score within ±1 noise floor of C212 (0.8350-0.8380), most likely about 0.837. Epoch time about 1.2-1.3x C212's. There is a small risk of slower convergence near epoch 50.

history.hypothesis: L43's trunk has no long-range mixing at its coarsest resolution, so the pair-pool and average readout see features with a limited receptive field. A zero-init dilated bottleneck stack (dilations 1-8 on 30 positions) gives each position near-whole-sequence context, as it does in the L46 and C222 trunks, and the bilinear readout can use it.
history.predicted_effect: Score about 0.8355 (within ±1 floor of C170's 0.8354). Early epochs track C174 closely because of the identity init. Epoch time rises by about 10%.

history.hypothesis: L46 loses fine positional detail through three max-pools before its per-output dilated stack. HRNet-1D's advantage comes partly from letting high-resolution features reach the coarse stream through max-pool and 1x1 links. Adding such zero-initialised lateral links lets the dilated FiLM stack use finer motif detail.
history.predicted_effect: Score of about 0.8370-0.8385, from 0 to +0.5 floors over C212. Epoch time rises by under 5%, and the run converges like the parent because the links start at zero.

history.hypothesis: C226 keeps C221's input_pipeline and loss, which build partner windows and a pair-delta loss term (pair_weight default 0.5). But C226's model sets torch._evoloop_pair to None and never sets _evoloop_pairpred, so the pair term is silently off and the partner windows are wasted. The lineages this recipe comes from train with the ref/alt delta supervised; C23's gain came with it. Restoring the term gives this structure the leader's full training objective and supervises single-base variant effects, which a sequential BiLSTM readout should be able to use.
history.predicted_effect: Validation mean R² about +0.003 over C226, from better calibration of single-base differences and the extra signal on paired rows. Training cost per step rises by up to about 1.5x.

history.hypothesis: Answers S68. Patience 6 gave +0.78 floors on C217 (C221), whose best epoch came late and was still improving. Patience 6 has also helped on most other lineages (C180 +1.11, C203 +0.87, C192 +0.63, C223 +0.54). C222's per-output dilated FiLM stack adds capacity, which should benefit at least as much from the longer schedule at each LR. If the two gains add, the result should beat C221.
history.predicted_effect: About 0.841 to 0.842 against C222's 0.8390. Most of the gain should be in late epochs, with SK-N-SH possibly helped by the per-output stack.

history.hypothesis: HRNet's global average pooling discards motif co-occurrence. L52's windowed bilinear pair pooling captures it, and adding it residually (zero-init) lets the trunk use it without disturbing the leader's start.
history.predicted_effect: The run trains like C217 for the first epochs, then lands within about a floor of it. My middle estimate is slightly below (around 0.837-0.839), since PairPool has not transferred to other trunks. SK-N-SH could gain most if cell-specific signal comes from motif combinations.

history.hypothesis: Rows with extreme measurement error (se above the 98th percentile in any cell type) carry label noise that the Student-t heteroscedastic loss only partly discounts. Removing them, as Malinois filtered its training labels, sharpens the fit, most of all for SK-N-SH, the noisiest cell type. If S51 holds, this treatment does not help either.
history.predicted_effect: The score lands within about 0.5 floors of C223, most likely slightly below it (about 0.8367). SK-N-SH changes most, in either direction, and K562 and HepG2 stay within 0.002 R².

history.hypothesis: Cell-type-specific signal in fine-scale motif features is lost because the fine streams reach the mapper identically for all outputs. A per-output channel FiLM on them before the nonlinear mapper lets each cell type weight different fine features, which mainly helps the harder SK-N-SH contrast.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R2 about +0.0006 over C222 (about 0.2 floors), with most of the gain in SK-N-SH (+0.001 to +0.002) and K562/HepG2 flat. Epoch time rises by under 5%.

history.hypothesis: L52's ceiling is its plain ResNet trunk. C221's multi-resolution HRNet-1D trunk, feeding the same windowed bilinear PairPool readout, mixup head and VAT, gives the readout better features. If VAT helps on HRNet (S69), this run beats C231, which is the same model without VAT.
history.predicted_effect: Validation R2 of about 0.8385 (between C223 at 0.8374 and C221 at 0.8404). Expected to land within 0.5 floors of C231, with roughly 1.5x C221's epoch time. Slower early epochs could put it near the epoch-50 cut threshold.

history.hypothesis: Fine-scale stage features are useful but differ in relevance per cell type. Summed into the shared coarse map before the dilated stack (C228), they cannot be weighted per output. Routing them around the stack with a per-output FiLM into the mapper, as in C233, lets each output use them separately.
history.predicted_effect: Validation mean R² of about 0.8385 (range 0.837 to 0.840), with the gain mostly in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, and epoch time up about 10%.

history.hypothesis: Uniform average pooling over the 30 coarse positions forces all three cell types to weight sequence regions identically. A softmax pool with per-output positional bias and a content score, both starting at zero, lets each output emphasise different regions and motifs. This should help mostly the smaller cell-specific part (SK-N-SH).
history.predicted_effect: Score about 0.8393 to 0.8400, about +0.2 floors over C222, with SK-N-SH R² rising slightly more than K562 and HepG2. Epoch time is essentially unchanged.

history.hypothesis: Patience 6 helped in 10 of 12 lineages, including the plain HRNet trunk, but it has never been run to the end on the leader because C230 was cut at epoch 50.
history.predicted_effect: Expected to be better than C233.

history.hypothesis: On C233 the mapper features are already specialised per output by FiLM. A bilinear motif-pair pooling of those per-output maps may capture cell-type-specific motif co-occurrence that average pooling loses, especially for SK-N-SH, which trails.
history.predicted_effect: Close to neutral: mean R2 within about 0.003 of C233 (0.8421), most likely slightly below. SK-N-SH R2 changes no more than the other cells. Epoch time rises by less than 15%.

history.hypothesis: S23's batch-256 optimum comes from the interaction of the per-step EMA horizon and the gradient noise. It should hold on the Student-t/VAT pair-pool model, but 512 is a milder step than 1024, so the cost should be smaller than C61's 4.09 floors.
history.predicted_effect: Validation R2 about 0.8346, roughly 0.8 floors below C223 (0.8374), with faster epochs and a best epoch reached later in epoch count. A score within one floor of C223 or above it would refute the sharp optimum for this family.

history.hypothesis: S36's failures came from heavy or indel-based augmentation, which shifts motif spacing and corrupts labels. A light, constant substitution noise (2 random substitutions inside the insert on 50% of training rows) acts as input dropout at the motif level. It should regularise the pair-pool readout without slowing convergence.
history.predicted_effect: Training loss slightly higher and the best epoch slightly later than C185; the epoch-50 check is passed. Final validation R² within one floor of C185, about 0.834, with SK-N-SH the most likely to move.

history.hypothesis: C233's fine-stream FiLM and C235's per-output attention pool specialise different things. The FiLM changes per-output channel weights of the shared fine features; the pool changes per-output position weights after the mapper. Combined, they should add roughly the larger gain plus a small part of the smaller.
history.predicted_effect: About 0.8425 to 0.843: slightly above C233 (0.8421), with SK-N-SH gaining most. Epoch time is essentially unchanged.

history.hypothesis: C233 gained +1.02 noise floors on the same HRNet-1D trunk (L53) from a zero-init per-output FiLM before the mapper. The cell-type-specific part of the signal is the harder part, and here a single shared embedding feeds all three outputs. A per-output FiLM on the 512-channel map lets avg pooling and PairPool form cell-specific co-occurrence features. With zero init the model starts exactly at C232's function. The head and every other module keep one set of weights, run on three modulated copies of one feature map, so this is not an ensemble.
history.predicted_effect: Validation mean R2 rises by about 0.0015, mostly in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, where the contrast part is larger.

history.hypothesis: Letting each output gate every stream's fused features before the final exchange's SiLU lets fine-scale, full-resolution features specialise per cell type through a nonlinearity. This should help the cell-type-specific contrasts, SK-N-SH most of all.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R2 about 0.843, roughly +0.3 floors over C233. SK-N-SH should gain the most, with epoch time up about 10-15%.

history.hypothesis: The fine-resolution streams carry cell-type-specific short-range motif information. In C233 each output can only rescale them linearly, so one nonlinear per-output layer, a dilated bottleneck with FiLM, lets each output build its own combinations of fine features.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R² about 0.8423-0.8430, against 0.8421 for C233, with the largest share of the gain in SK-N-SH. Epoch time rises about 10%. The run should not be cut at epoch 50, since the change starts as an exact identity of C233.

history.hypothesis: S65's stem gain came from a larger first-layer motif bank. If that is right, doubling C233's stem to 256 filters (kernel 15) lets the entry conv choose from more motif detectors before the full-resolution stream.
history.predicted_effect: Small change: score about 0.8423 (+0.1 floor), within ±0.5 floor of C233. SK-N-SH should move most if at all. Epoch time rises by under 10%.

history.hypothesis: L54's distinguishing part, a zero-init residual BiLSTM over the 30-position pooled features, could add order-aware long-range mixing to HRNet's coarsest stream. The dilated bottleneck stack provides receptive field but not recurrent, content-dependent integration. Placing it before the per-output stack lets every output and the attention pool use it.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R2 within one noise floor of C235, most likely 0.000 to 0.002 below it. Epoch time rises by about 10-15%. SK-N-SH changes by no more than the other cell types.

history.hypothesis: HRNet-1D's lead over pooled ResNets (C202, C229) comes from repeated fusion across the 1/2 to 1/8 streams, not from keeping a 96-channel stream at full 240-position resolution. Single-base detail is already captured by the stem's kernel-15 convolution before pooling.
history.predicted_effect: Score within about one floor of C233, most likely 0.3-0.5 floors below (around 0.8405-0.841). Epoch time drops by roughly a quarter to a third. SK-N-SH changes no more than the other two cell types.

history.hypothesis: Most of the cost of moving from batch 256 to 512 under EMA comes from the EMA averaging window doubling in samples. Halving the per-step EMA horizon (decay 0.998) at batch 512 restores the window, so the score should match batch 256 at about half the steps.
history.predicted_effect: Within about half a floor of C232 (roughly 0.838-0.840), at noticeably lower time per epoch; clearly better than the -1 floor that batch 512 alone cost on L52 (C240).

history.hypothesis: The zero-init per-output FiLM on the shared fine streams helps on its own, independent of the per-output dilated stack on the coarse stream. If so, adding it to plain HRNet (C221) gains about a noise floor, as it did on C222.
history.predicted_effect: Validation mean R2 about 0.840-0.841, roughly 0.003 above C221 and about 0.002 below C233. SK-N-SH should show the largest per-cell gain over C221.

history.hypothesis: The leader's per-output specialisation comes only after all cross-resolution fusion is done. Modulating each stream per output before the shared final exchange lets each cell type reweight how fine and coarse features combine through the exchange's nonlinearity. That could recover part of the SK-N-SH-specific signal.
history.predicted_effect: Score close to C233: about 0.841-0.843, mean around 0.8415. The gain should come mostly from SK-N-SH R² (+0.002 or so), with K562 and HepG2 flat. Epoch time should rise by about 10-15%.

history.hypothesis: L55 lacks per-output specialisation inside the trunk, and that is the part that separates the leader. Per-output dilated FiLM layers on the coarsest stream let each output build its own long-range features before the mapper, PairPool and head, which a FiLM on the mapped map cannot do.
history.predicted_effect: Validation R2 about 0.840 to 0.841 (+0.2 floors over C232). Most of the gain should be in the cell-type-specific part (SK-N-SH and HepG2 R2). Epoch time should be about 1.2x C239.

history.hypothesis: C219's shared readout makes all three cell types draw on the same 512-dim nonlinear head, which limits how much of the cell-specific contrast in the pair-pool features they can use. A zero-init per-output FiLM on the fused embedding, followed by one shared mean/logvar head run per output, lets each cell type reweight the features. This helped LegNet and is part of the leader.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R2 about 0.838 (+0.2 floors over C223), with most of the change in SK-N-SH and HepG2. Per-epoch time rises about 5%, since the head runs on 3B rows.

history.hypothesis: The higher-capacity HRNet trunk with its full-resolution stream may overfit the 40% training set more than L35's pooled ResNet does. Early sequence augmentation (indels plus point mutations, faded to clean data by epoch 16) could regularise the fine-scale stream without hurting the final fit.
history.predicted_effect: Validation is slower in the first 16 epochs, around 0.825 at epoch 20, then catches up after the fade. The final score is about 0.840, within a floor below C233, with SK-N-SH no better than now.

history.hypothesis: HRNet's lead over saturated trunks such as LegNet (S14) comes from keeping full-resolution features, and C249 showed that stream carries about 3 floors. Its single ResBlock per stage is then under-capacity, so more depth there, not width, should help.
history.predicted_effect: Score about 0.843 (+0.3 floors over C233), with most of the gain in HepG2 and K562. Epoch time rises by about 15%, and the curve tracks C235's early on because the new blocks start at zero.

history.hypothesis: PairPool on the 30-position final map mixes motif pairs over about 120 bp at 8-bp resolution. Reading the 60-position stage-3 pre-pool map (4-bp resolution, window of about 60 bp) should capture spacing-specific motif co-occurrence that the coarse map blurs, a gap S73 suggests matters.
history.predicted_effect: Score about 0.838, near C223 (0.8374). Small gains spread over all three cell types, with SK-N-SH the most variable. Epoch time rises by under 5%.

history.hypothesis: If S3 holds, per-row se adds nothing in the Student-t variance either. Without it, the learned log-variance absorbs the measurement noise and the means are unchanged in quality. My middle expectation is a slight loss, because se gives free per-row information on noisy rows. These matter most in SK-N-SH and under the var^beta weighting.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R2 within about 1 floor of C235, centred about 0.4 floors lower (about 0.8383). Any loss should be largest in SK-N-SH. Training should be as stable as the parent's.

history.hypothesis: The full-resolution stream carries position-precise motif information that the coarser streams cannot recover (C249). At 96 channels it may be too narrow to hold enough distinct motif detectors, while depth (C254) was not the limit. Widening it to 128 channels should let more motif features reach the exchanges and the mapper.
history.predicted_effect: The final score is within about half a floor of C233, slightly above (around 0.8423). The gain, if any, is spread across all three cell types. Epoch time rises by roughly 20-30%. The validation curve at epoch 50 stays within one floor of the lineage median.

history.hypothesis: C247 came back invalid with no diagnostics. The block uses torch and nn without importing them; it relies only on `import math` and `torch.nn.functional as F`. It also calls `.view` on expanded tensors, which fails when they are not contiguous. Its parts, C222/C233's per-output dilated FiLM stack and C239's per-output PairPool readout, each ran on their own. So a version that builds and runs cleanly should show what this structure can do. Answers the fair trial: fix what stopped it.
history.predicted_effect: The run trains to completion and scores close to C233/C239, perhaps slightly above, from per-output coarse-stream context.

history.hypothesis: The full-resolution stream carries about 3 floors of the score but sees only local context before it is pooled. Dilating its second ResBlock per stage (2,4,8,8) lets base-resolution features encode motif spacing up to about 65 bp at no extra parameters, and should add value where extra width or depth did not.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R2 within about ±0.003 of C233. If it gains, the gain is largest for HepG2 and SK-N-SH. Epoch time is unchanged.

history.hypothesis: If the BiLSTM in C229 carries real signal (long-range order of motifs), adding the same zero-init BiLSTM residual at C219's 30-position, 256-channel bottleneck will raise the score. If C229's level comes from its conv trunk and readout, the score stays within a floor of C223.
history.predicted_effect: Within one noise floor of C223, about 0.836 to 0.837, slightly below on balance. Epoch time rises by about 10%. The curve starts like C219 because of the zero init.

history.hypothesis: A low-weight distributional auxiliary (HL-Gauss cross-entropy over 128 bins) gives the shared HRNet head a richer gradient on the long right tail. That should improve the mean's calibration slightly, mostly in SK-N-SH, without slowing convergence.
history.predicted_effect: Final score within about one floor of C233. My middle estimate is 0.8405-0.842, with no early-stop cut. Most of any change would show in SK-N-SH R2.

history.hypothesis: Average-pooling the full-resolution and half-resolution streams down to 30 positions dilutes sharp, single-site motif responses. A max-pooled path keeps the peak strength of each motif inside a window and gives the readout information the coarse stream lacks.
history.predicted_effect: Gain of about 0.0 to 0.002 over C235, ending near 0.840-0.842. Any gain should be slightly larger in SK-N-SH and HepG2, the cell types that depend more on specific motifs. Epoch time should rise under 5%.

history.hypothesis: HRNet's ResBlocks mix information only locally (ks9) and through the exchanges. A global-context channel gate (squeeze-excitation, as in MPRA-LegNet) lets each stream reweight its motif channels by the whole-sequence context, for example suppressing cell-type-irrelevant motifs. Zero-init keeps optimisation identical to C254 at the start.
history.predicted_effect: Final score within about 1 noise floor of C233, most likely around 0.841-0.843. Epoch time should rise by under 10%, and the validation curve should match C254 for the first ~10 epochs. Any gain should be spread evenly across cell types rather than concentrated in SK-N-SH.

history.hypothesis: L52 loses fine-resolution detail through three max-pools before its readout. HRNet's lead comes partly from fusing average-pooled finer features (removing them cost about 3 floors in C249). Giving the coarse map zero-init laterals from the pre-pool stage outputs (240, 120 and 60 positions) should let PairPool and the BiLSTM see finer motif evidence.
history.predicted_effect: Validation mean R2 about 0.840-0.841, roughly +0.3 floors over C260. Gains should be largest on SK-N-SH and HepG2. Training should start identical to C260, with epoch time up under 10%.

history.hypothesis: VAT's input-space smoothness penalty regularises the HRNet trunk the way it did the dilated FiLM ResNet (C202, +0.55). C232's tie with C221 hid this because PairPool was added at the same time. Without PairPool, VAT alone should show its own effect.
history.predicted_effect: Epochs about 1.4-1.6x slower and a slower start (val near 0.826-0.829 at epoch 50, risk of an early cut). If it finishes, the final score is about 0.840-0.842, within a floor of C233, with no per-cell-type pattern.

history.hypothesis: Per S31, one extra zero-init residual block of late-stage depth (512 ch, ks5, at the coarsest length) between the mapper and the avg/PairPool readouts adds no measurable accuracy on HRNet-PairPool.
history.predicted_effect: Score within about ±0.003 of C232 (0.8396), most likely 0.8390-0.8400. Epoch time rises by under 10%. The curve looks like C232's.

history.hypothesis: Coarse-scale PairPool, at 30 positions with a window of about 120 bp, duplicates what the HRNet trunk already pools. Bilinear co-occurrence on the full-resolution stream, with a 31-bp window, captures base-pair-scale motif spacing and orientation that the 8x-pooled map has lost, giving the readout information the global average lacks.
history.predicted_effect: Final score near C232, from slightly below to slightly above (about 0.838-0.842). Gains, if any, should show more in the cell-type contrasts (HepG2/SK-N-SH r) than in K562. Epoch time rises by under 5%.

history.hypothesis: The trunk's coarse 30-position features have a limited convolutional receptive field before the BiLSTM and PairPool. C233's two zero-init dilated ResBlocks (dilation 2 and 4) give the LSTM and the pair readout richer local-to-mid-range motif context, which may help the cell-type contrasts.
history.predicted_effect: Final score within about one floor of C260, most likely about +0.1 floor (0.8395-0.840). Epoch time rises by under 5%, and the early curve tracks C260 because of the zero init.

history.hypothesis: Per-row se inside the Student-t variance is informative, and scale 1.0 is near-calibrated. Doubling it overstates the noise of high-se rows and flattens the loss on them through var^0.25 and the wider t. This underfits the noisier, often high-activity rows that dominate SSE in R².
history.predicted_effect: About 0.5 floors below C235 (about 0.838), spread roughly evenly across cell types, perhaps slightly worse in K562/HepG2 where se is relatively smaller. If it instead gains 1 floor or more, scale 1.0 is too low.

history.hypothesis: With mixup, VAT, EMA and weight decay 0.04 already in place, the Dropout(0.3) in the head over-regularises the fused avg+PairPool embedding. Removing it, as the leader has none, lets the head fit the cell-type contrasts better.
history.predicted_effect: Final score about 0.840-0.841, roughly +0.3 floors over C239. The training loss should fall slightly faster, and the gain should be largest on the SK-N-SH contrast axis. Convergence epoch should be similar.

history.hypothesis: HRNet's global average pooling discards pairwise motif co-occurrence. L43's windowed bilinear PairPool captures it. Reading it from the shared coarsest stream (320 ch, 30 positions, the analogue of L43's trunk map) and adding it as a zero-init residual to the pooled embedding lets the model use pair features without disturbing the tuned per-output path.
history.predicted_effect: Final score near 0.8405. It is about 0.3 floors below C237 and 0.5 below C233, within one floor either way. Epoch time rises by about 10%, and it should not be cut at epoch 50 because it starts identical to C237.

history.hypothesis: C260 ran at patience 3 with a mid-run dip, and patience 6 lifted this lineage before; the result decides whether L52 can reach 0.842.
history.predicted_effect: Expected to be better than C260.

history.hypothesis: C245 lost because the BiLSTM sat on the coarsest stream, inside the exchange fusion. On the fused 512-channel mapped map (30 positions, the same length where it gained +1.28 on the pair-pool ResNet), long-range order mixing adds information that global average pooling discards.
history.predicted_effect: Trains about 10% slower per epoch and starts identical to C221. I expect a final score of about 0.8405 to 0.8415, roughly 0.3 floors below C233. Finishing above 0.844 would support S79; finishing below 0.838 would show the BiLSTM hurts HRNet wherever it is placed.

history.hypothesis: Max-pooling in the exchange down-paths throws away where a motif sits within each pooling window and how strong its neighbours are. Learned depthwise stride-2 convolutions, as in the original HRNet, should pass coarser streams better-summarised fine features. That helps the coarse per-output dilated stack, which reads them.
history.predicted_effect: Roughly parity with C233: final score 0.8405-0.8440, epoch time up under 5%, and no early cut.

history.hypothesis: HRNet fuses across resolutions only through local convolutions and 1x1 exchanges. Long-range ordered interactions across the 30 coarse positions are therefore modelled weakly. A BiLSTM residual on the fused 512-channel map supplies this, as it did on the pooled ResNet map in L52. This position avoids the cost seen when the BiLSTM sat on the coarse stream before the fine streams were merged (C245).
history.predicted_effect: The run converges like C235 early on, because the BiLSTM starts as an identity residual, and ends near 0.841 to 0.843. The per-epoch cost rises by about 30-50%. A gain above one floor is unlikely.

history.hypothesis: C248's 2.92-floor loss mostly came from the shorter EMA (0.998) together with the larger batch. With EMA decay kept at 0.999, the averaging window doubles in samples to about 512k, which smooths more. Batch 512 at the same lr then costs only a little, as on the pair-pool ResNet (C240, -0.1).
history.predicted_effect: Final score about 0.838-0.841, roughly 0.8 floors below C233. Epoch time about 40% shorter. The curve should be smooth, unlike C248's unstable one. A drop of 2 floors or more would instead confirm that 256 is the optimum on HRNet.

history.hypothesis: The HRNet trunk overfits the 40% training subset: added readout capacity does not help, while regularisers on the embedding (mixup, EMA) were what paid. Stochastic depth on the trunk ResBlocks regularises the multi-resolution features without adding parameters, and should give a slightly better validation optimum.
history.predicted_effect: Slower climb before epoch 50, possibly 0.002 behind C244 at that point. The best epoch comes later, and the final score lands near C233 (0.840 to 0.844), with the gain largest in SK-N-SH, the noisiest cell type.

history.hypothesis: If extra depth does not reliably help (S31), the two dilated (d=2,4) ResBlocks on the coarsest 320-ch stream are close to redundant. The receptive field they add is mostly already supplied by the per-output dilated bottleneck stack (dilations 1,2,4,8) on the same stream.
history.predicted_effect: The score should land within about 0.5 floors of C235 (around 0.839-0.840), with epoch time down roughly 5%. A drop above 1.5 floors would refute S31 for this trunk.

history.hypothesis: VAT adds about 1.5x epoch cost on HRNet-PairPool without helping: S66 found it neutral on non-dilated trunks and slow to converge on HRNet. Removing it should keep the score within noise while making epochs much cheaper.
history.predicted_effect: Seed-0 score within ±0.003 of C232 (around 0.839-0.841), with epoch time down about 35%.

history.hypothesis: HRNet's multi-resolution trunk resolves single-base differences better than the pooled ResNet. Supervising the predicted ref-minus-alt difference on training pairs might therefore give a sharper base-level signal here than on L50, where it was neutral.
history.predicted_effect: Within noise of C233 or slightly below: final score about 0.840 (-0.5 floors). Epoch time about 1.3-1.6x. There is a modest chance of being cut at epoch 50 if early convergence lags.

history.hypothesis: Nearest-neighbour upsampling in the exchanges copies each coarse feature over 2, 4 or 8 positions on a fixed grid. Fused fine streams then carry step artifacts that do not move with the ±10 bp training shift. Linear interpolation makes the coarse-to-fine path smooth and closer to shift-equivariant. This should give a slightly better fine-stream representation at no cost in parameters or speed.
history.predicted_effect: Same epoch time and parameter count as C221. The validation curve should track C221 closely, and the final score should land within about one floor of C233, near 0.842, with no cell type moving more than the others.

history.hypothesis: HRNet fuses across resolutions only through local convolutions and 1x1 exchanges. Long-range ordered interactions across the 30 coarse positions are therefore modelled weakly. A BiLSTM residual on the fused 512-channel map supplies this, as it did on the pooled ResNet map in L52. This position avoids the cost seen when the BiLSTM sat on the coarse stream before the fine streams were merged (C245).
history.predicted_effect: The run converges like C235 early on, because the BiLSTM starts as an identity residual, and ends near 0.841 to 0.843. The per-epoch cost rises by about 30-50%. A gain above one floor is unlikely.

history.hypothesis: LegNet's ceiling near 0.834 comes partly from its EfficientNet-style block: depthwise convolution with SE has less local cross-channel mixing than a full two-conv ResBlock. Putting that block into HRNet's stages should pull HRNet down toward LegNet's level.
history.predicted_effect: About 1.5 noise floors below C233, near 0.8375. Training should be slightly slower to converge. It should still pass the epoch-50 check, but possibly near the cut line. It should not fall below 0.834, because the multi-resolution layout and readout are kept.

history.hypothesis: The leader's gain came from per-output modulation of the shared fine-resolution features before the mapper. C254 lacks that and specialises only the coarse stream and the pool. Adding the zero-init fine-stream FiLM lets each cell type reweight fine motif channels, which is where cell-type-specific signal is.
history.predicted_effect: Final score about 0.8425, roughly +0.3 floors over C233. SK-N-SH should gain the most, and epoch time should be essentially unchanged.

history.hypothesis: Manifold mixup of the pooled per-output embedding was carried over from small LegNet trunks. On the larger HRNet trunk, already regularized by EMA, weight decay 0.04, shift and RC augmentation, it may blur the per-output contrast features and slow fitting more than it prevents overfitting, as VAT removal (+0.29, C280) hinted on the sibling trunk.
history.predicted_effect: I expect a validation score within about one floor of C235, most likely slightly below (around 0.8385). Peak validation should come a few epochs earlier, and per-cell Pearson should change little, with SK-N-SH most sensitive. A gain above 0.8425 would mean mixup was costing.

history.hypothesis: Per-output specialisation of the shared fine-stream features (C233's sh_film) is a real gain. It is compatible with the per-output attention pool, because the pool weighs positions while the FiLM reweights channels per cell type.
history.predicted_effect: Ends near C233 (0.840 to 0.843), about 0.5 to 1 floor above C235's 0.8395. Epoch time is unchanged.

history.hypothesis: C260's BiLSTM gain came from giving the bilinear PairPool readout context-mixed features at the 30-position bottleneck. HRNet's mapper map feeding PairPool in C232 is the same kind of map (512 ch, 30 positions), so the same zero-init residual placed there should help, unlike C245, where it sat inside the trunk.
history.predicted_effect: Roughly flat against C232, about -0.3 floors (0.8387). Epoch time rises by about 15-25%. A gain above +1 floor would contradict S10's family restriction.

history.hypothesis: Global average pooling over the 30-position per-output map dilutes strong single-site activators, which make up the long right tail of the labels. A zero-init per-channel gated max-pool term lets the readout weight peak responses without changing the starting point.
history.predicted_effect: Same training curve as C237 early on. The final score lands within about one floor of C233, slightly below on balance. Any gain should show as a small rise in Pearson r and R² for K562 and HepG2, where the high-activity tail is largest. Epoch time is unchanged.

history.hypothesis: The auxiliary MSE term is computed in the tempered PC space, where the contrast axes are up-weighted relative to how per-cell R² weighs them. Expressing it in the original label space, normalised by each cell's label variance, aligns the point-estimate pressure with the score. The Student-t term still handles noise and outliers.
history.predicted_effect: Mean R² within a floor of C233, about −0.2 floors. Any gain should show as better scale and offset calibration (MSE improving more than Pearson r), most likely in SK-N-SH, whose variance and noise differ most from the shared axis.

history.hypothesis: Forcing strand invariance inside the network removes the strand-specific signal that random RC augmentation lets the model use as implicit regularisation and extra variety. It also doubles compute per step. I expect it to lose against RC augmentation plus test-time averaging on HRNet, as it did on LegNet (S45).
history.predicted_effect: Slower early convergence. The score at epoch 50 should sit about 0.005-0.01 below the lineage median, with a real chance of being cut. If it finishes, the final score should be about 0.836 (around -2 floors vs C233), with epoch time about 1.9x.

history.hypothesis: Settles whether a 9x larger trunk wants more weight decay than the LegNet optimum (C80 cost 2.83 on LegNet).
history.predicted_effect: Expected to show no difference from C233.

history.hypothesis: Settles whether stronger shift augmentation, a regulariser that costs no time, helps the trunk that C285 shows benefits from regularisation.
history.predicted_effect: Expected to show no difference from C233.

history.hypothesis: Long-range interactions between coarse positions (motif grammar across the 240-bp window) are only reached through convolutions and dilations in C244. One zero-init self-attention layer over the 30 per-output coarse positions, as in L30, could add that interaction.
history.predicted_effect: Starts identical to C244. Final score within about a noise floor of C233, most likely slightly below (about 0.841), at roughly 10% more epoch time. A cut at epoch 50 is possible but unlikely, since the layer starts as the identity.

history.hypothesis: If the 10M HRNet overfits the 40% training set, as S82 suggests, input-level corruption may generalise better on held-out chromosomes. Each training position is replaced with probability 0.05 by an uninformative base (0.25 on every channel), which pushes the model to rely on redundant motif evidence rather than on single exact bases. This regularises without slowing convergence the way trunk-level changes did.
history.predicted_effect: The validation score lands within about one noise floor of C237, near 0.840-0.842. The peak epoch moves somewhat later, and training loss rises slightly at equal epochs.

history.hypothesis: The 10M HRNet's late layers over-fit the 40% training set under settings tuned for the 1M LegNet. Dropout of 0.3 in the shared 512-unit head, as used in L55, adds regularisation where mixup already shows a gain (S81) without slowing convergence of the trunk.
history.predicted_effect: The peak arrives a few epochs later and is about 0.001 higher than C233's 0.8421. Because the dropout acts on the mean and the logvar head together, the SK-N-SH R² should move most.

history.hypothesis: Training only in PC-rotated, temper-whitened space misweights errors relative to the score, which is mean per-cell R² in original units. An auxiliary MSE on (mu - y) mapped back through the inverse rotation and divided by each cell's label SD aligns the gradient with the metric. C290 gained from this on C283; it should help C244 the same way.
history.predicted_effect: About +0.0015 over C244 (0.8403 to about 0.842), so roughly 0.4 floors below C290. Most of the gain should show in SK-N-SH R², the cell type that contributes most to the contrast PCs. The epoch of the best checkpoint should be roughly unchanged.

history.hypothesis: On the 10M HRNet, a weak supervised ref/alt delta term (weight 0.25, computed on unmixed predictions) adds no signal beyond the plain regression loss. Its rows are single-base variant pairs whose label deltas are mostly measurement noise, so S13 should hold here too.
history.predicted_effect: Final score within about one noise floor of C244 (0.8403), most likely slightly below, around 0.839-0.841. Epoch time rises by about 1.3-1.4x, and the epoch-50 trajectory sits about 0.001-0.002 below the lineage median.

history.hypothesis: Decoupled weight decay at 0.04 is applied to every parameter. On this trunk that includes the zero-init per-output FiLM tables (film, films.*.emb, sh_film.emb), cell_bias, the BN gains (several zero-init on residual branches) and the biases. These are low-dimensional scale and offset parameters, and decaying them toward zero restrains per-output specialisation and residual branch gains rather than overfitting capacity. Exempting them while keeping decay on the weight matrices should let the FiLM paths express cell-type contrasts.
history.predicted_effect: Final score within about one floor of C237, slightly higher (around 0.8415-0.843). The learned FiLM gain norms should end visibly larger than in C237. The peak epoch should be similar or a few epochs earlier.

history.hypothesis: The 10M HRNet trunk overfits the 268k training rows under regularisation tuned for a 1M model. Dropping whole channels (p=0.1) of the shared 512-channel mapped map in training should reduce co-adaptation of the features feeding the per-output pools. It complements the manifold mixup that S81 shows still pays on this trunk.
history.predicted_effect: The best epoch moves later by about 5-15 epochs and the train-val gap narrows. Final score is about 0.841 (within a floor of C257), with roughly a 1-in-3 chance of beating it by more than 0.003.

history.hypothesis: Cell-type-specific signal partly sits in fine-grained motif detail that the shared full-resolution stream averages away. The step adds a per-output FiLM followed by a nonlinear residual conv on that stream, before pooling. This gives each output its own fine-resolution features, which a post-pool affine (sh_film) cannot express.
history.predicted_effect: Within noise of C290, most likely about 0.842 (-0.3 floors). Epoch time rises about 10-15%. Any gain should show mostly in SK-N-SH and HepG2 R², the more cell-specific outputs, rather than K562.

history.hypothesis: A 128-bin HL-Gauss cross-entropy on the rotated targets, as an auxiliary to the Student-t mean/variance loss, gives the shared head a richer distributional gradient and regularises the large HRNet trunk, as it did on the LegNet branch model.
history.predicted_effect: Score within about 0.003 of C233's 0.8421, most likely 0.840-0.843. Epoch time is essentially unchanged, and the peak epoch is similar or slightly later.
